title: Echopoint prod held: the gate's transport rerun did not know an SSE reset
summary: The echopoint post-deploy gate for echopoint#864 failed on two TCP resets from the gate runner to the dev edge. One reset was a `Could not connect to` error, which the gate reruns. The other was `SSE stream read error … connection reset by peer`, which the gate's transport regex did not know, so the gate failed without a rerun and prod stayed on 9264c31b. The routine's own suite script had learned the SSE class on 2026-11-09, but the copy of the rule in the gate was never updated. The fix adds the SSE class to the gate and a sample self-test, and the routine now checks its samples against the gate regex before every run. This is a regression of the [2026-11-05 gate transport resets](http://nanostack-dev-1340p:4320/postmortems/01a1ae3d-6e68-7cfc-9fcd-d5a3847a180b) postmortem: its fix did not cover this class.

impact.text: No customer impact. Prod echopoint did not get echopoint#864 (log-level fix for invitation refusals); every later echopoint change waits behind the next green gate. Dev was deployed and healthy.

trigger: At 21:38:50Z a TCP reset broke the SSE stream of `echopoint: secret outputs (cloud)` node `await-child`; at 21:41:10Z the gate's rerun step refused to rerun it as a non-transport failure.
detection: The deploy-failure alert job ran at 21:41:20Z, but nobody acts on it overnight. The routine found the red gate at its 2026-11-14T00:08Z run, when it reads every Deploy Router gate since the last run.
resolution: ci-workflows now counts `SSE stream read error … connection reset by peer` as transport and fails the step if its regex stops matching a known sample. Prod catches up at the next green echopoint gate (the routine does not rerun gates: a rerun promotes to prod).

whys.problem: The echopoint gate for #864 went red on TCP resets and held prod on 9264c31b

because.text: The rerun step classified the `secret outputs (cloud)` failure as not transport, so it reran nothing
because.evidence: Gate log: `Flows failed on more than a transport error: 6d952ea9-2dae-46f5-8dd5-3b8553315af2` (infra run 43512401138, job 132186071342)

because.text: The gate regex has no clause for `SSE stream read error … connection reset by peer`
because.evidence: `transport='Could not connect to|Connection refused by|TLS handshake|Could not resolve host|Request to [^ ]+ timed out'` in echopoint-test.yml

because.text: The routine learned the SSE class on 2026-11-09 in run_suites.sh, but nobody updated the gate's copy
because.evidence: run_suites.sh comment: `2026-11-09T20:0xZ: … an SSE reset during a dev deploy were left FAILED`; no ci-workflows change since #42 touches the regex

because.text: Two copies of the transport rule live in two repos, and nothing checks that they agree
The gate regex carries no list of the messages it must match, so nobody can see which classes it covers
because.evidence: echopoint-test.yml before this fix: regex only, no samples or test

because.text: A transport class reaches the gate only after it has failed a gate: the gate has no sample self-test
Two connections from the gate runner to the dev edge 172.64.80.1 were reset within 40 s
because.evidence: Gate log lines 471 and 475; same path as the 2026-11-05 resets and ledger row 76 (2026-11-09, 11-12)

because.text: The path from 1340p (192.168.2.18) to the Cloudflare edge resets connections every few days, cause unknown
because.evidence: 2026-11-05 postmortem action A5 is still open

because.text: Nobody has found why the 1340p path to the Cloudflare edge resets connections (A5 of the 2026-11-05 postmortem)
Prod stays held until the next echopoint merge, and nobody noticed for 2.5 h
because.evidence: No Deploy Router run after 43512401138 up to 2026-11-14T00:08Z; prod /health 9264c31b

because.text: A red gate is final: only a manual rerun or the next merge promotes, and the routine must not rerun gates
because.evidence: Routine Run notes: `The routine does not rerun a failed gate job (a rerun promotes to prod).`

because.text: Nothing owns a gate that is red only on transport errors: no automatic retry of the suite, no rule that lets the routine rerun it

contributing: The gate decides on the first failure message of a flow only; a second reset on a known class would not change the verdict.
The deploy-failure alert lands in Discord at night with nobody to read it.

well: The gate's TRANSPORT-RERUN logic and leak report from the 2026-11-05 postmortem worked for the known class.
Every `always` cleanup in both failed flows completed, so nothing leaked.
wrong: A fix to one transport classifier was not carried to the other the same day.
The 2026-11-05 fix was marked verified on two green gates that had no SSE reset, so verification proved nothing about this class.
lucky: The held change was a log-level fix; a security fix held the same way would have stayed off prod for hours.
The reset `POST /flows` in `integration operation outputs` ran in a throwaway org that its cleanup deleted, so a flow applied before the reset leaves no live resource.

actions.what: Add the SSE reset class to the gate regex and a sample self-test that fails the step when the regex stops matching a known transport message
run_suites.sh preflight fetches the gate workflow and checks each of its own transport samples against the gate regex; prints GATE-TRANSPORT-DRIFT
flow-suite-testing skill: a transport class added to one classifier is added to the gate and its samples the same run
Find why the 1340p path to 172.64.80.1 resets connections (carried over from 2026-11-05 A5)
Decide who reruns a gate that is red only on transport errors after its rerun: an automatic suite retry, or a rule that lets the routine rerun it

messaging.internal: Echopoint gate for #864 went red on two TCP resets; the SSE reset was not in the gate's transport list, so it did not rerun and prod stayed on 9264c31b. Gate regex fixed with a sample self-test; prod catches up at the next green echopoint gate.
